alternatives: Record and verify an equivalent immutable dependency resolution artifact in CI.
userDecisions: Confirm which package manager and lockfile CI and production must use.
rules.plainLanguage: The project names its dependencies but does not record the exact versions used to build it.
rules.consequence: A later install can select different package versions, making security review and repeatable deployment less reliable.
rules.confidenceBoundary: The rule confirms that a supported manifest has no adjacent or applicable workspace lockfile. It does not prove a malicious dependency or exploitable vulnerability.
rules.applicability: Supported package.json or pyproject.toml project roots, including declared JavaScript workspaces.
falsePositiveCauses: A lockfile is generated only in a deployment system outside the audited source.
An unsupported package manager records resolution in another file.

proposal.summary: Generate and commit the lockfile used by CI and deployment.

proposalRisks: A newly generated lockfile can select versions that differ from the current deployment.
sideEffects: Dependency versions or transitive packages may change when the first lockfile is generated.
rules.securityRetest: Rerun the source audit and confirm the manifest is covered by a supported lockfile.
rules.functionalRetest: Run the normal install, build and project test commands using the committed lockfile.
rules.rollback: Revert the lockfile if the locked install or application tests regress, then reconcile the deployed dependency set before regenerating it.

alternatives: Use an approved narrow Gitleaks suppression for a proven non-secret fixture.
userDecisions: Confirm whether the match is a live credential and whether repository history may be rewritten.
rules.plainLanguage: A pinned Gitleaks rule matched secret-shaped material in Git history.
rules.consequence: If the value is a live credential, anyone with repository history access may be able to use it.
rules.confidenceBoundary: The match and redacted fingerprint are recorded. Credential validity, exposure and authorization are not tested.
rules.applicability: A Git worktree with the caller-installed tested Gitleaks version.
falsePositiveCauses: A test or revoked value matches a secret pattern.
A generated example intentionally resembles a credential.

proposal.summary: Validate privately, revoke any live credential and remove it from current and historical source where appropriate.

proposalRisks: History rewriting disrupts existing clones and references.
sideEffects: Credential rotation can interrupt services; history rewriting requires repository coordination.
rules.securityRetest: Rerun the pinned Gitleaks history scan and confirm the fingerprint is absent or covered by an approved suppression.
rules.functionalRetest: Verify every service using a rotated credential can authenticate and complete its normal health check.
rules.rollback: Do not reactivate a leaked credential; roll back application configuration to a separately issued valid credential if rotation breaks service.

alternatives: Use an approved narrow suppression for a proven non-secret fixture.
userDecisions: Confirm whether the match is live and which secret store should replace it.
rules.plainLanguage: A pinned Gitleaks rule matched secret-shaped material in the current files.
rules.consequence: If the value is live and later committed, built or shared, it may grant unauthorized access.
rules.confidenceBoundary: The match and redacted fingerprint are recorded. Credential validity and distribution are not tested.
rules.applicability: A readable project directory with the caller-installed tested Gitleaks version.
falsePositiveCauses: A placeholder or test value matches a secret pattern.
A local ignored file contains intentionally non-production data.

proposal.summary: Validate privately, revoke any live credential and remove it from source and build inputs.

proposalRisks: Credential rotation can interrupt dependent services.
sideEffects: Local development and CI need a replacement secret-injection path.
rules.securityRetest: Rerun the pinned Gitleaks directory scan and confirm the fingerprint is absent or approved.
rules.functionalRetest: Run dependent service authentication and the project tests with replacement credentials.
rules.rollback: Do not restore a leaked value; use a separately issued credential if the replacement fails.

alternatives: Use an authenticated, access-controlled remote debugging tunnel for an explicitly approved incident window.
userDecisions: Confirm whether the script is used outside local development and whether remote debugging is required.
rules.plainLanguage: A package script asks the Node debugger to listen on every network interface.
rules.consequence: If that script runs on a reachable host, someone who reaches the debugger may inspect secrets or control the process.
rules.confidenceBoundary: The package command is present. The audit does not prove the script runs in production or that the debug port is reachable.
rules.applicability: String-valued package.json scripts using --inspect or --inspect-brk with 0.0.0.0 or [::].
falsePositiveCauses: The script is limited to an isolated local container.
Network policy makes the listener unreachable.

proposal.summary: Bind the inspector to loopback and keep debug scripts out of reachable production processes.

proposalRisks: Remote debugging workflows can stop working after the bind address changes.
sideEffects: Container or remote development debugging may require an explicit secure tunnel.
rules.securityRetest: Rerun the source audit and verify the deployed process exposes no public inspector listener.
rules.functionalRetest: Run normal start and approved debugging workflows in their intended environments.
rules.rollback: Restore the debug workflow only behind verified network isolation if approved debugging becomes impossible.

alternatives: Apply an upstream-supported backport or isolate the affected feature until an upgrade is available.
userDecisions: Confirm whether the affected feature is used and whether update, isolation or time-bounded acceptance is appropriate.
rules.plainLanguage: OSV-Scanner linked a recorded dependency version to one or more public vulnerability advisories.
rules.consequence: If the application uses the affected code path, an attacker may be able to trigger the behavior described by the advisory.
rules.confidenceBoundary: Package identity, version and advisory IDs matched. Reachability, exploitability and local severity are not inferred.
rules.applicability: Supported lockfiles or dependency manifests accepted by the caller-installed tested OSV-Scanner version.
falsePositiveCauses: The vulnerable code path is not reachable in this product.
The advisory does not affect the product configuration or platform.

proposal.summary: Review advisory applicability, then update, replace or time-bound an explicitly owned suppression.

proposalRisks: Dependency upgrades can introduce API, behavior or transitive-dependency changes.
sideEffects: Build output, runtime behavior or compatibility can change after the dependency update.
rules.securityRetest: Rerun OSV-Scanner and confirm the advisory identity is absent or explicitly accepted with an owner and expiry.
rules.functionalRetest: Run the project test suite and the user journeys that depend on the upgraded package.
rules.rollback: Revert the dependency change if functional tests regress, then choose a supported mitigation without marking the advisory fixed.

alternatives: Generate hidden maps in a private build step and prevent them from entering public artifacts.
userDecisions: Confirm whether production error monitoring requires source maps and where private maps may be stored.
rules.plainLanguage: The build configuration asks for browser source maps that can reveal original source structure if they are published.
rules.consequence: Public maps can expose source code, comments and internal names that make later attacks easier.
rules.confidenceBoundary: The configuration enables map output. The audit does not prove a map was built or served publicly.
rules.applicability: Recognized Next.js, Vite, Nuxt, Svelte and Astro JavaScript/TypeScript configuration files.
falsePositiveCauses: Maps are uploaded only to an access-controlled monitoring service.
The production artifact pipeline removes maps before publication.

proposal.summary: Disable public production source maps or keep them only in an access-controlled monitoring service.

proposalRisks: Browser production debugging and readable error stack traces may become less useful.
sideEffects: Error monitoring needs a private source-map upload step to preserve symbolication.
rules.securityRetest: Rebuild and verify no public .map response or embedded source map is available, then rerun the source audit.
rules.functionalRetest: Run the production build, load the application and confirm error monitoring still symbolicates as intended.
rules.rollback: Restore private map generation if observability regresses, while keeping public artifact delivery blocked.

alternatives: Keep a placeholder-only .env.example and inject real values through the deployment secret store.
userDecisions: Confirm whether the file contains live values and where each environment should obtain replacements.
rules.plainLanguage: A file named like a real environment configuration is present. The audit does not read its contents.
rules.consequence: If the file contains live credentials and is committed or published in a build artifact, an attacker may gain access to services or data.
rules.confidenceBoundary: Filename presence is a lead only. Repository tracking, contents, credential validity and public delivery are not established.
rules.applicability: Files named .env or .env.<environment>; documented example, sample, template, dist and defaults files are excluded.
falsePositiveCauses: The file contains only non-sensitive local settings.
The file is ignored and never copied into an artifact.

proposal.summary: Verify tracking and artifacts without printing values, then move live secrets outside source and builds.

proposalRisks: Changing environment injection can break local development, CI or deployment startup.
sideEffects: Developers and deployment jobs may need a new documented secret-injection path.
rules.securityRetest: Verify the file is absent from Git history and built artifacts, without exposing its contents, then rerun the audit.
rules.functionalRetest: Start the application in development and its deployment-like test environment with the replacement configuration path.
rules.rollback: Restore the prior configuration source only in a private environment if startup fails; do not recommit a live secret.

rules.plainLanguage: Some eligible files could not be read or the bounded scan stopped early, so missing findings cannot be treated as a clean result.
rules.consequence: A security issue may exist in files the audit did not inspect.
rules.confidenceBoundary: The coverage ledger proves an input was skipped, truncated or unreadable. It does not prove a vulnerability in that input.
falsePositiveCauses: A deliberately excluded large or unreadable file is irrelevant to the application.
A conservative traversal limit stopped after all relevant files were already scanned.

proposal.summary: Review coverage reasons, restore readable inputs or raise an allowed bound, then rerun.

proposalRisks: Higher traversal limits consume more time and memory and may include unrelated files.
sideEffects: The next audit can take longer and produce additional findings.
rules.securityRetest: Rerun with the same subject and scope until all required source rules have completed coverage.
rules.functionalRetest: No product code change is required; confirm the audit still targets the intended project root.
rules.rollback: Restore prior traversal limits if resource use becomes unacceptable, and record the remaining evidence as unknown.

rules.plainLanguage: The built-in audit could not find a supported project manifest, so it could not establish which source checks apply.
rules.consequence: Relevant source risks may remain unchecked until the stack is identified.
rules.confidenceBoundary: This proves only that supported Node or Python manifests were not found inside the bounded traversal.
falsePositiveCauses: The project uses an unsupported language or non-standard manifest.

proposal.summary: Record the stack manually or add a reviewed adapter before drawing source conclusions.

proposalRisks: Expanding source scope can increase review time and expose additional local paths in sanitized evidence.
sideEffects: A new adapter or wider scope may add findings that were previously outside coverage.
rules.securityRetest: Provide a supported manifest or adapter and rerun until applicable source checks report coverage.
rules.functionalRetest: No product change is proposed; verify only that project discovery still identifies the intended root.
rules.rollback: Remove an incorrect stack override if it causes the wrong files or framework rules to be selected.
